body_es: Trunk-based development es un modelo donde todo el equipo integra su trabajo directamente en una única rama principal (el "trunk", normalmente `main`) de forma muy frecuente, en lugar de mantener ramas de larga vida. Cada rama de trabajo vive solo unas horas o, como mucho, un par de días: se crea, se hace el cambio, se abre un PR pequeño y se fusiona de vuelta antes de que diverja demasiado del trunk. Esto reduce casi a cero los conflictos de integración masivos que aparecen cuando una rama vive semanas separada de las demás. El requisito para que funcione es un pipeline de CI/CD robusto que valide cada cambio en minutos, porque no hay tiempo para una revisión larga sin bloquear a los demás. Para publicar trabajo incompleto sin romper producción, se usan feature flags: el código llega al trunk y se despliega, pero permanece oculto tras una bandera hasta que está terminado. Un error común es adoptar trunk-based development sin invertir primero en tests automatizados sólidos; sin esa base, integrar tan seguido significa llevar bugs a producción constantemente en lugar de reducir el riesgo, que es justamente lo que este modelo busca evitar frente a GitFlow.
body_en: Trunk-based development is a model where the whole team integrates its work directly into a single main branch (the "trunk," usually `main`) very frequently, instead of keeping long-lived branches. Each working branch lives for only a few hours or, at most, a couple of days: it is created, the change is made, a small PR is opened, and it merges back before it diverges too much from the trunk. This reduces to almost zero the massive integration conflicts that show up when a branch lives separated from the others for weeks. The requirement for this to work is a robust CI/CD pipeline that validates every change within minutes, because there is no time for a lengthy review without blocking everyone else. To ship incomplete work without breaking production, feature flags are used: the code reaches the trunk and gets deployed, but stays hidden behind a flag until it is finished. A common mistake is adopting trunk-based development without first investing in solid automated tests; without that foundation, integrating this often means constantly shipping bugs to production instead of reducing risk, which is exactly what this model aims to avoid compared to GitFlow.
example_code:
from datetime import date, timedelta


class TrunkBranch:
    def __init__(self, name, created, feature_flag=None):
        self.name = name
        self.created = created
        self.feature_flag = feature_flag
        self.merged = None

    def merge(self, day):
        self.merged = day
        return (self.merged - self.created).days


branches = [
    TrunkBranch("fix-button-style", date(2026, 9, 20)),
    TrunkBranch("new-checkout-flow", date(2026, 9, 21), feature_flag="checkout_v2"),
]

for b in branches:
    lifetime = b.merge(b.created + timedelta(days=1))
    status = "oculto tras feature flag" if b.feature_flag else "visible de inmediato"
    print(f"{b.name}: vida de {lifetime} día(s), {status}")

max_lifetime = max(
    (b.merged - b.created).days for b in branches
)
print(f"vida máxima de rama: {max_lifetime} día(s)")
print("todas por debajo de 2 días:", max_lifetime < 2)
example_output:
fix-button-style: vida de 1 día(s), visible de inmediato
new-checkout-flow: vida de 1 día(s), oculto tras feature flag
vida máxima de rama: 1 día(s)
todas por debajo de 2 días: True
